findings.title: add_members returns 500 for existing members and can partially apply
findings.description:
`add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for each name. `Group#add` is `self.users.push(user)` (app/models/group.rb:272-274). The `group_users` table has a UNIQUE index on `(group_id, user_id)` (db/migrate/20130416004933_group_users.rb:9), so pushing a user who is already a member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. The action does not rescue it. `ApplicationController`'s `rescue_from Exception` logs and re-raises (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:62-74), so the request ends in a 500. Each `push` commits on its own, so names earlier in the list stay added and the rest are skipped.

The old `usernames=` path diffed against current members (app/models/group.rb:248-263), which avoided this. The new spec only adds users who are not yet members (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:98-108). Re-entering an existing member is an ordinary admin action, so this should block merge. Fix: skip existing members before pushing (for example, `next if group.users.exists?(user.id)`) and run the loop in a transaction.

findings.title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove, leaving user_count and primary_group_id stale
findings.description:
`group.users.delete(user_id)` on a has_many :through deletes join rows in bulk in Rails 4.1.8, so `GroupUser` destroy callbacks don't run. That skips the `counter_cache: "user_count"` decrement (app/models/group_user.rb:2), so `groups.user_count` stays too high. The admin list reads that column (the index spec checks `user_count`).

`Group#remove` (app/models/group.rb:276-278) destroys each join row, so it does run the callback. The diff removed the controller's other caller of `remove` (the old `update_patch`). The old PUT path also cleared stale primary groups through `destroy_deletions` (app/models/group.rb:286-295, line 291). The new path doesn't, so a removed member keeps `primary_group_id`. `PostSerializer#primary_group_name` (app/serializers/post_serializer.rb:96-102) does not check membership, so the removed group's name still appears on that user's posts.

Fix: call `group.remove(User.find(user_id))` and clear `primary_group_id` when it points at this group. Add a spec that checks `user_count` after removal.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one at exact multiples, and "next" can reach an empty page
findings.description: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and limit 50 it reports 2 pages, and with 100 members it reports 3. The correct value is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. Because `showingLast` stays false on the real last page, "next" runs. Line 33 then clamps the offset to `user_count`, so the admin lands on an empty "3/3" page. Fix: use `Math.ceil`, and clamp the next offset to `(totalPages - 1) * limit` instead of `user_count`.

findings.title: findMembers clamps against a stale total, so deleting the last row on the final page leaves an empty page
findings.description: The clamp `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)` uses the total from the previous fetch. `removeMember` calls `findMembers()` (line 47) before the total is refreshed. Take 51 members with the admin on page 2 (offset 50) and remove that member. The request uses offset 50, the server returns an empty page with total 50, and the UI stays on an empty page 2 with no step back. Fix: after the response, if `offset >= total` and `total > 0`, move the offset to the start of the last page and fetch again.

findings.title: The public members page shows only the first 50 members, with no pager
findings.description: Before this diff, `GroupsController#members` returned every member of a non-automatic group. Now `findMembers()` requests offset 0 with the default limit of 50. `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` has no pager or load-more. The group index already uses the `LoadMore` mixin (`views/group-index.js.es6`), so there is an existing pattern to follow. Any group with more than 50 members now shows a truncated list with no way to see the rest.

findings.title: GroupsController#members trusts limit and offset: negative values return 500, and limit is uncapped
findings.description: `params[:limit].to_i` and `params[:offset].to_i` go straight into the query. A negative value makes PostgreSQL reject the query (LIMIT or OFFSET must not be negative), which surfaces as a 500. Nothing caps `limit`, so one request can return a whole large group. Reading an uncapped list was already possible for non-automatic groups, but the negative-value 500 is new on that path. Fix: clamp `limit` to a range such as 1..100 and `offset` to at least 0.

findings.title: Add and remove failures are silent in the admin UI
findings.description: `removeMember` and `addMembers` attach no failure handler. In the model, `addMembers` and `removeMember` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-60) only chain a success `findMembers()`. A 422 for an automatic group, a 404 when removing a non-member, or the 500 above all leave the admin with no message. `save` and `destroy` in the same controller show `bootbox.alert` on failure (lines 84-87 and 103-105). The TODO at line 62 notes that the input is not cleared after a successful add. Fix: add a rejection handler that calls `bootbox.alert`, and clear `usernames` on success.

findings.title: create drops alias_level, which the JS sends
findings.description: `Discourse.Group#create` posts `asJSON()`, which includes `alias_level` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:62-75). The action sets only `name` and `visible`, so the alias level chosen for a new group is discarded and saved as the default 0. The old `create` had the same gap, so this predates the diff, but the diff rewrote this action and kept the gap. Fix: add `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?`, matching `update` at line 37, and cover it with a spec.

findings.title: The public members endpoint has no working test for its new response shape
findings.description: `members` now returns `{members:, meta:}`. The only pagination spec (lines 71-85) is `pending` and expects a bare array, so it cannot pass against the new shape. The example labelled "calls `posts_for` and responds with JSON" (lines 65-69) calls `:posts`, so no example checks the members JSON or its `meta` values. Fix: replace the pending spec with one that asserts on `members` and `meta` (`total`, `limit`, `offset`).

findings.title: The admin spec misses the failure modes this diff introduces
findings.description: Not covered: adding a username that is already a member (the FAIL above); unknown or non-member usernames in `add_members` (the removed PATCH tests covered this); `user_count` and `primary_group_id` after `remove_member`; and non-automatic renames and `alias_level` changes in `update`. The `.update` example (lines 49-60) hardcodes `id: 1` and asserts `visible == true`, which may already hold before the request, so it can pass without showing that the write happened.

findings.title: Group#usernames= has no production caller after this diff
findings.description: The old controller used the setter. The new controller doesn't. The only remaining callers are specs (spec/models/group_spec.rb:137-157 and spec/models/user_spec.rb:1011-1022). Remove it with those specs, or keep it and document why.

findings.title: add_members assumes a string, and whitespace around commas silently drops users
findings.description: `params.require(:usernames).split(",")` raises NoMethodError (500) if the client sends an array or hash. A list written as `"alice, bob"` keeps the leading space, so `User.find_by_username` misses `" bob"` and the user is skipped without a message. Fix: check the parameter type, and `strip` each name.

findings.title: Unrelated churn, small inconsistencies, and accessibility gaps
findings.description: Whitespace-only reformatting in this template and in `admin-group-selector.hbs`, re-indented `protected` methods and `find_group`, and `ilike` changed to `ILIKE` are unrelated to the feature. Smaller issues: `create` strips the name but `update` does not (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:40). `Group#destroy` has a stray `};` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:82), and `findMembers` has `return ;` (line 21). In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs`, `<label for="name">` (line 7) and `<label for="alias">` have no matching `id`, because the `text-field` and `combo-box` calls set only `name`. Prev and next (lines 16 and 18) and the remove control in `group_member.hbs:1` are `<a>` elements with no `href`, so keyboard users cannot reach them.

findings.title: Admin endpoints remain admin-only
findings.description: The new `members` routes sit inside `resources :groups, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` in the staff admin namespace. `Admin::GroupsController` inherits `ensure_staff` (app/controllers/admin/admin_controller.rb:3-4, 13-15). The public `members` action still uses `find_group`, which calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!`.

findings.title: CSS move keeps badge and group form styling intact
findings.description: The `.form-horizontal` rules that were removed sat inside the `.badges` block (around line 400 in the new file), and the diff's `section.details` hunk header is only git's context label. They now live in a shared `.groups, .badges` block (lines 164-182). `groups.hbs` and `badges.hbs` use those roots, so their styling is unchanged, and no other admin page loses styling.
